text:
Senator Tuberville honors David Bedford as August Veteran of the Month
E. S. Jensen
U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville recognized U.S. Army Chief Warrant Officer David Bedford of Wilmer as the August "Veteran of the Month," according to an Aug. 4 announcement from his office.
Tuberville released a video highlighting Bedford's military service and community involvement. “When it comes to the military, there is no such thing as working 9 to 5. You are on call 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. For U.S. Army Chief Warrant Officer David Bedford of Wilmer, he still has this mentality about serving others,” Tuberville said in his remarks.
Bedford, a Mobile County native, learned about military service from his father, who was a World War II veteran and Purple Heart recipient. In 1969, Bedford enlisted in the Army and trained as a pilot at Fort Rucker before deploying to Vietnam in 1971. He flew Huey helicopters for more than 1,500 hours on resupply and transportation missions during his deployment. “He describes his most satisfying missions as those where he brought mail to troops on the frontlines — a small way to help put a smile on their faces during a very dark time,” Tuberville said.
Beyond his military career, Bedford is active in several organizations supporting veterans and their families. He and his wife Theresa are members of the Christian Motorcycles Association and participate in outreach activities with other veterans through their shared interest in motorcycles. He is also involved with the Patriot Guard Riders, supporting Gold Star families.
“It is my honor to recognize David Bedford as the August ‘Veteran of the Month,’” Tuberville said.
Constituents can nominate Alabama veterans for future recognition by submitting information to Senator Tuberville’s office for consideration in upcoming "Veteran of the Month" series via email.
Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and serves on committees including Armed Services; Agriculture; Veterans’ Affairs; Health, Education, Labor & Pensions; and Aging, according to the official website. His office assists Alabamians with federal agencies and constituent needs. Tuberville built a four-decade career coaching college football teams such as Auburn before entering public service.
